newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah rises on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah rises on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah rose against the dollar in active early trading on Friday on tight liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
They said the tight supply triggered off selling in value today dollars which also dragged value spot down to a low of 2,323.25 before it rebounded on profit-taking to 2,324.0/25.0.
Spot rupiah opened at 2,325.5/26.5 to the dollar.
Dealers said swap premiums also edged up slightly.
One local bank dealer said liquidity suddenly turned very tight. "State banks seemed to have started the dollar unloading after they were caught in the tight condition," he said.
However, the dealer said the tightness was not expected to last long because operators would use short-term securities (SBPUs) later to obtain some funds from the central bank.
Dealers said apparently higher-than-expected weekly tax payments had caused the tight conditions.
"Swap premiums are edging up slightly but it wasn't that drastic," another dealer said.
He expected the dollar-rupiah rate to range between 2,324.0 and 2,326.0 for the rest of the day.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were quoted at 2,323.75/24.50 and 2,321.0/22.0, respectively.
Overnight swap rose to 2.75/2.90 from 1.25/1.75 points on the back of tight liquidity. Tom/next swap was at 0.50/0.52.
One-month swap was quoted 16.0/16.5, two at 32.75/33.75, three at 48.50/49.5 and six at 97.50/99.00 points.
Dealers said sentiment remained firm on the rupiah after the central bank widened its intervention band to eight percent from five percent on Wednesday.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,309/2,501 and the conversion rate at 2,309/2,357 on Thursday.
